learningObjective: Distinguish self-attention from cross-attention by tracing which sequence supplies Q, K, and V and predicting the resulting attention-matrix shape.
mediumRationale: A compact deterministic SVG is the smallest medium that can keep source-to-projection arrows aligned with square and rectangular score matrices, making routing and shape inspectable together at phone width.

mediumComparison.mermaid: Rejected because a flowchart can show where X and Y enter but cannot express the 3-by-3 versus 2-by-3 matrix shapes precisely without awkward labels.
mediumComparison.svg: Selected because fixed source nodes, projection arrows, and discrete matrix cells expose both sequence ownership and the resulting score dimensions.
mediumComparison.semanticHtml: Rejected because a comparison table could list Q/K/V sources and shapes but would not spatially connect each source to its projections and output rows.
mediumComparison.interaction: Rejected because changing sequence lengths would add controls before the stable routing rule is learned; two fixed examples are sufficient.
mediumComparison.paperReuse: Rejected because the original Transformer architecture figures are much denser than this narrow comparison and the arXiv non-exclusive distribution license does not grant general figure reuse. No source figure, coordinates, prose, or layout is copied.
mediumComparison.noVisual: Rejected because the formulas state the source difference but require readers to mentally route three projections and infer why one score matrix is square while the other can be rectangular.

pages.insight: The preceding text-representation slide contrasts encoder-style and decoder-style pretraining but contains no Q/K/V routing.
The memory-network slide distinguishes an embedded query from context memories, providing conceptual background but not transformer self- versus cross-attention.

The central transformer slide states that decoder self-attention reads previous decoder output while its next attention sublayer takes queries from the decoder and keys and values from encoder output. This is the most directly relevant deck page.
The adjacent BERT and SAN slide names self-attention and cross-attention for separate sentence representations but does not trace Q/K/V ownership or matrix shape.
The following transformer-family slide discusses multi-head attention, causal language modeling, scaling, and normalization without clarifying cross-attention routing.
A later optimization slide gives standard self-attention with Q, K, and V all shaped by the same n and emphasizes its square n-by-n score matrix; it contains no cross-attention comparison.

sourceReview.notes: The hardest prose-only mental model is that self- and cross-attention use the same computation but route tensors from different sequence owners. The original schematic uses X with three tokens for self-attention, so QK-transpose has three query rows and three key columns. Cross-attention uses two X queries and three Y key-value pairs, producing two-by-three scores and two output rows. This also makes clear that K and V must share the source-length axis. Source review prompted two related precision fixes: decoder-only prompt RAG usually uses self-attention rather than a separate retrieval cross-attention path, and cross-attention masking is not inherently causal merely because the query side is autoregressive.

agentReview.summary: Read the complete article, text-indexed all 214 deck pages, inspected the transformer neighborhood and later self-attention formula, checked the original Transformer paper and official PyTorch documentation with their licensing terms, corrected two routing-adjacent claims, and reviewed the original matrix geometry.

implementation.accessibility: The SVG has a linked title and detailed description naming each sequence owner, token count, projection source, score shape, and output-row rule. Direct X/Y and Q/K/V labels, arrows, panel headings, and discrete cell counts carry all meaning without color. The 360-unit viewBox has no minimum width and uses established 11-pixel SVG text primitives for readability at 390 CSS pixels. Existing theme variables preserve dark-mode contrast, and shared print rules enforce a light high-contrast palette and keep the figure together.
